body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (5) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Approved design says builders push, build state says they never do 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability
>
>Description >
> >
>v1.md still makes builders push their task branches when done (Build step 2) and relies on that
>for STOP recovery, while the BUILD-STATE.md decision table and Finding A say builders never push
>and the lead merges worktree branches locally. A fresh session is told to read v1.md first and
>then this file, so it can follow either instruction.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/v1.md[111]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5/files#diff-2b52e99c393c109f0060898a48e99b807bac479fa6f867b8e9b985ed76357204R111-R111) > >```diff >+2. **Build:** builders take the tasks, at most three at once, each in its own worktree and task branch, which they push when done. The lead answers their questions from the docs or escalates, merges their work into the mission branch and runs the checks. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>v1.md is declared the source of truth ('edit by PR'), yet the decision made in this same PR
>(builders never push, to address Finding A) is recorded only in the build-state file. The design's
>STOP and PAUSE rules (lines 267-268) also assume builders push task branches, so the two documents
>describe different builds.
>
> > [docs/design/v1.md\[111-111\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L111-L111) > [docs/design/v1.md\[268-268\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L268-L268) > [docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md\[55-56\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md/#L55-L56) > [docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md\[66-66\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md/#L66-L66) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The approved design `docs/design/v1.md` says builders push their task branches (Build step 2, line 111) and that a running builder can push to its task branch on STOP (line 268). `docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md` records the decision 'Builders work in local worktrees and never push' (Finding A). A resuming session reads v1.md first and may follow the superseded process. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/v1.md[111-111] >- docs/design/v1.md[266-268] >- docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md[55-56] > >## Recommended Fix >Edit v1.md so builders work in local worktrees and never push; the lead merges worktree branches locally. Update the STOP and PAUSE rules to match, and reword the 'pushes a task branch' references. Either record the change as an explicit CHANGE to the approved design or state in v1.md that BUILD-STATE supersedes it for the build. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c5233d74-f7ee-467d-816c-44a7ea97bc09?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c5233d74-f7ee-467d-816c-44a7ea97bc09)

2. Watchdog loses its builder-progress signal 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The watchdog rule in v1.md counts a builder push as progress, but the build-state decision removes
>builder pushes. The watchdog therefore relies only on recorded-step changes, so a lead making real
>progress through builders with no step change for three hours is reported as LEAD-SILENT and
>buzzes Matthew.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/v1.md[266]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5/files#diff-2b52e99c393c109f0060898a48e99b807bac479fa6f867b8e9b985ed76357204R266-R266) > >```diff >+- **Watchdog:** a recurring scheduled task, created by the architect at the phase's kickoff and deleted at `DONE`. It measures progress, not chatter. Every three hours it checks whether the recorded step changed or a builder pushed. If neither happened in three hours, it posts `LEAD-SILENT` and buzzes, unless the step is `waiting for owner` or the phase is paused or stopped. It catches a dead lead, a successor that never started, a lead stuck in a loop, and a waiter stopped by an idle machine. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The watchdog definition says it checks 'whether the recorded step changed or a builder pushed'. The
>decision row 'Builders work in local worktrees and never push' removes the second signal, so the
>watchdog's progress measure no longer matches what the pipeline does.
>
> > [docs/design/v1.md\[266-266\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L266-L266) > [docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md\[66-66\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md/#L66-L66) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The watchdog progress test in `docs/design/v1.md` (line 266) treats 'a builder pushed' as progress. `docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md` decides builders never push, so that signal is gone and the watchdog can only see recorded-step changes. A lead working through long builder tasks would be reported as silent. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/v1.md[266-266] >- docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md[66-66] > >## Recommended Fix >Change the watchdog's progress signal to what still happens: recorded-step or MISSIONS.md changes, plus `STATUS` posts or commits to the state branch. Then update the sentence about the watchdog catching a stuck lead to match. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/06313873-b12e-4dc5-b6de-c063c8fd2f55?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/06313873-b12e-4dc5-b6de-c063c8fd2f55)
3. Preflight passes any 403 as no branch protection 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>Finding B records that preflight treats the GitHub 403 'upgrade to Pro' answer as 'no protection'
>and passes it. A 403 caused by missing permissions or a token scope problem would be treated the
>same way, so the approving-review check passes without being able to read the rules.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md[59]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5/files#diff-eb974eadcb2e1d4f382c2409c07a470b3df0574298ed8eda187eb1a6d7b1375fR59-R59) > >```diff >+- **B. Private repos on GitHub Free can't have branch protection or rulesets** (the API answers 403, "upgrade to GitHub Pro"). Preflight treats that answer as "no protection", which passes. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The preflight check 'main requires no approving review' is designed to read protection state and
>fail when unreadable. Accepting every 403 as a pass means an unreadable protection state is reported
>as a pass, which weakens the guard the design depends on.
>
> > [docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md\[59-59\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md/#L59-L59) > [docs/design/v1.md\[241-241\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L241-L241) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md` (Finding B) says preflight treats the GitHub 403 'upgrade to Pro' answer as 'no protection', which passes. The rule is generic: any 403 is taken as a pass, including permission or scope failures where protection cannot be read. The check in `docs/design/v1.md` (line 241) is meant to confirm that no approving review is required. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md[59-59] >- docs/design/v1.md[241-241] > >## Recommended Fix >In the preflight spec, pass only when the 403 body names the plan limit on a private repo. Report any other failure as 'could not verify', so Matthew decides instead of the check passing silently. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/fe55fbb7-98ba-41f6-8d68-4463709b8094?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/fe55fbb7-98ba-41f6-8d68-4463709b8094)
4. Review exemption by directory lets code skip coverage 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>The coverage rule exempts everything under reviews/ from review, decided by path rather than by
>file type. Code placed under that directory would be merged with no review, and the gate would not
>see it as a change needing coverage.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/v1.md[143]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5/files#diff-2b52e99c393c109f0060898a48e99b807bac479fa6f867b8e9b985ed76357204R143-R143) > >```diff >+**Coverage rule.** Every code change in a PR is covered by a review before merge. Coverage is about code, not commits: review records under `reviews/` aren't reviewed, so committing a report never triggers another review. Each review records the commit it covered. Code changed after the last covering review gets a scoped cold review, which focuses on those changes but sees the whole PR diff, so it can catch interactions with earlier code. That covers fixes after cold round 2, fixes after Qodo's final re-review, and a re-review that never arrives. A scoped review doesn't count as a round, and a top-severity finding from it goes to Matthew. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The coverage rule says 'review records under reviews/ aren't reviewed', and the merge gate checks
>that 'every code change' is covered. Because the exemption is keyed on the directory, a builder's or
>fix commit adding a script under reviews/ would merge unreviewed.
>
> > [docs/design/v1.md\[143-143\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L143-L143) > [docs/design/v1.md\[58-58\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L58-L58) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`docs/design/v1.md` (line 143) exempts `reviews/` from coverage by directory alone. Review records are committed under `reviews/cold/M/` and `reviews/qodo/PR-/` (line 58). Any executable or source file placed under `reviews/` would merge without review, and `room.py gate` would not require coverage for it. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/v1.md[143-143] >- docs/design/v1.md[58-58] > >## Recommended Fix >Define the exemption by file pattern (for example `reviews/**/*.md`) and state that any other path under `reviews/` is code. Have the gate treat non-report files under `reviews/` as changes that need coverage. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/4e75349d-6191-4e19-b08d-bcaed96380b4?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/4e75349d-6191-4e19-b08d-bcaed96380b4)

5. Platform-check checkboxes contradict recorded results 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability
>
>Description >
> >
>The 'To verify' checklist in v1.md still shows all eleven assumptions unchecked, while
>BUILD-STATE.md records several as Pass. A reader following v1.md alone would think the platform
>assumptions are untested.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/v1.md[R364-366]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5/files#diff-2b52e99c393c109f0060898a48e99b807bac479fa6f867b8e9b985ed76357204R364-R366) > >```diff >+- [ ] The lead can merge a PR through Claude's GitHub proxy, naming the expected head commit. >+- [ ] Sessions can push `mission/*`, task branches and `agent-room/state` through the proxy, or a required prefix (such as `claude/`) has to be adopted. >+- [ ] Preflight can read branch protection, rulesets and admin bypass through the proxy. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>BUILD-STATE.md marks assumptions 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 as Pass, but the matching items in v1.md
>remain '- [ ]'. The build plan in v1.md also still says the platform check is a spike in a scratch
>repo, while the recorded results come from this repo.
>
> > [docs/design/v1.md\[364-374\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/v1.md/#L364-L374) > [docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md\[39-51\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea58582b24d52a886e1661351c0f8193d57b4865/docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md/#L39-L51) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The 'To verify' checklist in `docs/design/v1.md` (lines 364-374) is fully unchecked, while `docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md` records Pass for assumptions 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8. The build plan (line 391) also describes a scratch-repo spike, which is not how the platform check was run. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/v1.md[364-374] >- docs/design/v1.md[391-391] >- docs/design/BUILD-STATE.md[39-51] > >## Recommended Fix >Check off or annotate each item in v1.md with a pointer to its result in BUILD-STATE.md, and reword step 2 of the build plan to match where the check was run. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/af2c5040-cd9e-4342-840b-15b1b9a6d589?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/af2c5040-cd9e-4342-840b-15b1b9a6d589)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
